Back what grows.

The readers in full

Grade 3, English, then grade 4, Urdu. Reading on a phone, a grown-up beside the second child. 2026.

How we measure

Every term, our children and children in nearby schools sit the same test.

Reading

Low-fee schools, 2022 to 2024: 64% of our children read at grade level, 41% in the schools next door. Half as many again.

Maths

When maths fell behind the comparison schools, we sent the quiz home to parents on WhatsApp.

Islamabad

Against similar government schools we had not reached: a gain of 0.28 standard deviations.

A full trial

A comparison group chosen by lot, independent assessors, the plan written before the results.

Working with the government

Not one thing: we learned who was in the government, and gave it the credit.

The people

Thousands of officials tracked; an advocacy team won them over one at a time.

The brand

The programme carries the government's name. The credit is theirs; the politics stays off us.

The data

Every officer sees which schools and teachers need help, and where improvement is happening.

Promotion

The government rewrote its teacher promotion policy on our data. One teacher in our district received a national award.

Today

Islamabad, paid since 2023: 422 schools, 4,000 teachers. Rawalpindi: 261 schools, about $3 a child. Balochistan and Sindh: pilots.

Learning per dollar: the method

For every hundred dollars, how many years of good schooling does a child gain?

The table

86 programmes, each with a trial behind it, ranked by learning per hundred dollars. World Bank researchers, 2023.

The top

The first five rows train no teachers. Among programmes that work through teachers, Argentina's is first, at 15.4.

Known ones

Kenya's national structured teaching, 4.9. Brazil's classroom coaching, 2.65, the closest cousin of ours.

Our figure

8.3, an estimate: 0.2 standard deviations a year at $3 a child. Eleventh on the whole table; lower on an all-in cost.

The target

20: first among programmes that work through teachers.

Why the problem exists

Every child is born with the same potential. Three layers around them decide what happens to it.

The home

Parents who could not go to school themselves, working long hours, often speaking a different language from the one the school teaches in.

The teacher

Trained once in fifteen to twenty years. Fifty children in the room. No structured materials for teaching reading.

The government

Policy that changes with every government, and no data on which children are learning and which are not.

Taleemabad builds the thing that makes all three pull the same way for the child.
